title: Review of c46's driven-prey fuel fork: replicated on seed 4; the fuel cut dissolves every prey body (23 -> 0 by t=6500 without predators, 22 -> 0 by t=7000 with them) while the prey material is conserved, and predator material grows
summary: World copied unchanged; labkit seed 4, 128^2, 70 frames (t=7000). Fed run: 22 prey and 23 predator bodies at t=6000, 21 and 23 at t=7000. Fork at t=6000 (fork_t 6000): prey bodies 22 -> 11 (t=6200) -> 4 (t=6500) -> 0 (t=7000); predator bodies stay 23 and mean predator material rises 0.035 -> 0.081 on the freed prey. Predator-free fork (pred_t 1e9): prey bodies 23 -> 17 (t=6200) -> 0 (t=6500), mean prey material 0.254 before and after (conserved). Bodies counted as connected prey a > 0.5 (counts.txt).

observations.E: counts.txt: predator-free fork 23 -> 0 prey bodies by t=6500 with mean prey material 0.254 unchanged; with predators 22 -> 0 by t=7000 while the fed run keeps 21-22; the prey matter is never made from fuel, so the dependence is on the fuel-driven condensation

seeds_run.result: pass: all prey bodies dissolve after the fuel cut in both arms, matter conserved

controls_run.E: rerun/fed_seed4 (fed twin from the same seed) against rerun/fork_seed4 and rerun/fork_nopred_seed4

verdicts.limitation: One new seed; with predators the last prey body goes between t=6500 and 7000, slower than the finding's 500 t; my fork arms are separate runs from t=0 with the same seed (deterministic), not branches of one saved state. A global cut, not a per-individual one.
